findings.evidence: `Trichotomy.lean:147` supplies the shared strong context. Mathlib `TensorPower/Symmetric.lean:42` defines `SymmetricPower.tprod` and `span_tprod_eq_top` over `[CommSemiring R] [AddCommMonoid M]`, while `ExteriorPower/Basic.lean:42` supplies `ιMulti` and `ιMulti_span` over `[CommRing R] [AddCommGroup M]`; `G` does not occur at all in declarations 150–219.
findings.fix: Split the section: state lines 150, 168, 179, 199 over `[CommSemiring k] [AddCommMonoid V]`; lines 159, 173, 189, 211 over `[CommRing k] [AddCommGroup V]`; and add `[Group G]` only to the dual-invariance and invariant-form declarations (with the corresponding semiring/ring assumptions).
findings.issue: The shared `[Field k] [Group G] [AddCommGroup V]` context over-restricts every declaration in `Squares`: the square-to-form maps and injectivity/symmetry lemmas do not use `G`, while the symmetric side needs only a commutative semiring and the exterior side only a commutative ring; the invariant symmetric and `apply_of_mem_invariants_dual` lemmas likewise do not require a field.

summary: The square-to-form API remains unnecessarily restricted to fields, groups, and additive groups, despite its constructions having substantially more general Mathlib signatures.
